rulings.reason: As written the judge scores only where a request points, and the closing clause ('Score the anchoring, not the merit of the change requested') affirmatively forbids weighing what the request establishes. A one-line unsupported demand citing a paragraph number scores 10 while a data-rich comment that names only the topic scores 5, so the induced ordering tracks citation convention rather than substantive merit. Provision-level citation is a professional-drafting fingerprint heavily confounded with whether the commenter had counsel, which is a declared Track B channel. Admitting it to the A bank would credit the articulated scorecard with document shape and inflate apparent closure, the more dangerous error here.

To score this the judge must locate concrete particulars in the text -- workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, compliance-process -- and no surface tell, letterhead, or boilerplate can manufacture a high score. That content is the feasibility and implementation evidence notice-and-comment exists to elicit: it is what the comment establishes about how the rule would actually operate, not the form it takes. It correlates with submitter type but does not score identity, since an insider letter with no particulars scores 0 while any commenter supplying real operational particulars scores 10. The residual weakness is that granularity is not explicitly required to bear on the proposed provisions, but the substantive side clearly dominates the instruction as written.
